question: Which forestry practices (partial harvesting versus clearcutting, retained woody debris, riparian retention) maintain biodiversity or speed its recovery in Canadian forests?

cause.label: Forestry practices (partial harvesting, clearcutting, retained woody debris, riparian retention)

edges.subject: Harvest disturbances
edges.sentence: Conversely, 77.4% of harvest areas and 57.4% of areas disturbed by wildfire were considered as recovered by all three metrics.

edges.subject: Recently partially harvested stand
edges.object: Increased proportion of native decumbent hemicryptophytes dispersed by animals or birds
edges.sentence: Recently partially harvested stands had a significantly higher proportion of exotic, wind-dispersed hemicryptophytes and of native decumbent hemicryptophytes dispersed by animals or birds than old growth stands.

edges.subject: harvesting disturbance
edges.sentence: Harvesting disturbance was associated with an increase in total number of species, both at clearcut and downstream unharvested sites compared to the reference forests

edges.subject: Time elapsed after clearcutting and slashburning
edges.sentence: Species richness increased in all zones (ESSF, *n* = 2; ICH, *n* = 2; and SBS, *n* = 6) between the first year after burning (44, 39, and 58 species respectively) and the end of the monitoring

edges.subject: Woody debris presence
edges.sentence: Richness was highest (DMRT; P = 0.05) in the piles and windrows with the piles and dispersed also being similar, and these three treatments higher than the forest sites.

edges.subject: Clearcutting and slashburning
edges.sentence: For all zones combined, richness increased from 79 species in year 1 to 132 species 20 years after clearcutting and slashburning.

edges.subject: Woody debris presence
